oneRepMaxes.note: GOAL max (target), not a verified current 1RM — Plan!A8 says week 11 singles confirm/update them. Every %TM in the Program sheet multiplies this cell.

loadFormula.note: Column I is an array formula in all 77 percentage-driven rows. Squat rows point at Plan!$B$5, bench at $B$6, deadlift at $B$7. INDIRECT("H"&ROW()) is just a self-referential way of saying "the %TM cell on my own row".

exercises.name: Bench volume — Larsen press (no leg drive)
exercises.notes: LARSEN = flat bench with FEET UP / unsupported (on bench or straight out), no leg drive, normal comp grip and full ROM. It is NOT the JM press (skull-crusher negative into a close-grip press) - that is a triceps/lockout tool and belongs with close-grip work, not here. Feet-up costs most lifters 5-15% vs comp bench, so expect ~310-325 max. Wk5 is a calibration week: load to last-set RPE.

unrepresentable.concept: Target RPE alongside a % or absolute load
unrepresentable.where: column J (Tgt RPE), on all 191 prescribed rows
unrepresentable.note: THE BIG ONE. LoadPrescription is an either/or enum, but the sheet prescribes BOTH on 110 of 203 rows (77 percent-based + 33 absolute), and Plan!A23 makes the relationship explicit: "% is the anchor, RPE is the governor. If the target beats the RPE cap that day, drop weight and hit the RPE." The enum forces you to throw one away. Recommend a separate PlannedSet.targetRPE: Float? field so RPE is a cap that composes with any load kind, rather than a third mutually-exclusive case.

unrepresentable.example: columns A (Week 1-12) and B (Meso 1-3); grey fill FFEAEAEA marks weeks 4, 8, 12
unrepresentable.where: columns A, B and row fill colour
unrepresentable.note: WorkoutBlock keys its program by absolute Date only. There is no week index, no mesocycle grouping, and no per-week theme/deload flag. The sheet is also date-free: it says "Week 3, Fri", never a calendar date, so importing requires choosing a block start date and projecting.

unrepresentable.concept: Sets-x-reps as a prescription (rather than N enumerated sets)
unrepresentable.note: The sheet writes one row per exercise with a set count; PlannedExercise wants an array of PlannedSet. Expanding 6x3 into six identical PlannedSets (done here) loses the authored intent and makes editing "make it 5 sets" a multi-object operation.

unrepresentable.example: Rows 2/3: "Bench press — heavy" (Notes "Top set") then "Bench — back-off (paused)"
unrepresentable.note: SetType is warmup/working/drop only. A back-off is neither a drop set nor an ordinary working set, and here it is modelled as a SEPARATE exercise row with its own name, so the app would import it as a second PlannedExercise for the same lift rather than as typed sets of one exercise.

unrepresentable.example: Plan!A27 "Warm up thoroughly; mobility as you see fit"
unrepresentable.note: The sheet prescribes zero warmups — every row is a working set. SetType.warmup has no source data here, so an importer cannot populate it.
No numeric rest column exists. The one rest instruction in the whole sheet is a RANGE (60-90s) buried in a note; PlannedSet.restTime is a single Int. Every restTime in this export is null.

unrepresentable.example: Row 10: "Walk with wife (recovery)" — no sets, no reps, no load
unrepresentable.note: Exercise has only name + muscleGroup, and PlannedExercise expects sets. A recovery walk has duration/distance, not sets and reps. Exported here as an exercise with an empty sets array, which is representable but meaningless.

unrepresentable.where: baked into column D exercise names
unrepresentable.note: No tempo field anywhere in the model. Pause duration and deficit height are encoded in free-text exercise names, which means the catalog has to carry a separate Exercise entry per variation (24 distinct names for what is really ~10 movements x modifiers).

unrepresentable.concept: Percentages anchored to a GOAL max, not a current 1RM
unrepresentable.example: Plan!B5 = 495 for squat, described in Plan!A8 as a target, not verified
unrepresentable.note: LoadPrescription.percentOf1RM resolves against User.maxLifts, i.e. the lifter's ACTUAL max. This sheet resolves against an aspirational goal max. Importing naively would silently reprice the whole block against a different (lower) number. Needs either a per-block training-max override or an explicit "planning max" distinct from maxLifts.

unrepresentable.where: column I formula, all 77 percent rows
unrepresentable.note: The sheet rounds every computed weight to the nearest 5 lb. LoadPrescription.resolvedWeight does raw multiplication with no rounding, so app-computed weights will show values like 264.625 lb where the sheet shows 265.

unrepresentable.concept: Per-exercise coaching notes vs. per-set notes
unrepresentable.example: Row 79: a 400-character note explaining what a Larsen press is and is not
unrepresentable.note: PlannedExercise.notes exists, so this fits, but the sheet uses one note per exercise-per-week (the same exercise gets a different note in week 5 vs week 7). Notes are week-scoped instructions, not properties of the exercise.

unrepresentable.example: Plan!A25: "OHP + bench variations use DOUBLE PROGRESSION on literal loads (not %): hit all sets x reps at or under target RPE, then add weight"; row 32 note "5 when all sets hit reps @ target"
unrepresentable.where: Plan!A25 and column N on rows 32, 33
unrepresentable.note: A progression RULE, not a static prescription. Nothing in the model represents "if condition then add X lb next week". This is the part that most wants the phase-2 coach.

unrepresentable.example: Plan!A24: singles-triples = RPE 6-8, fives = RPE 8, compound 8-10s = RPE 7-8, isolation 8-12s = RPE 9-10
unrepresentable.note: Block-level policy that explains every RPE number in column J. WorkoutBlock.notes is a free String, so it can be stored but not acted on.

unrepresentable.example: columns K/L/M — "Act Wt", "Act Reps", "Act RPE" (all empty in this file)
unrepresentable.note: Maps cleanly onto WorkoutSet (weight/reps/rpe). Worth noting only because the sheet interleaves plan and log in one grid, whereas the model splits them into program/workouts — and the owner has clearly been logging elsewhere (Strong) and pasting results back into column N as prose.

unrepresentable.example: "Chest-supported row (or seal row)", "Incline press (BB or DB)", "Lat pulldown / cable row + face pulls"
unrepresentable.note: One row can mean "pick one of these" or even "do all of these" (the lat pulldown row bundles pulldown + row + face pulls into one line). Exercise is a single catalog entry; there is no notion of a substitution set or a bundled accessory slot.

Reported here for completeness: the sheet contains NO superset markers. No A1/A2 labels, no merged cells, no grouping shading, no conditional formatting. Fill colours encode day-of-week and deload only (verified against the legend in row 206). PlannedWorkout.exercises' nested-array superset support is unused by this program — every group is a group of one.

extractionNotes: All 12 weeks are written out explicitly, row by row. Nothing is derived, inherited, or templated — week 7 Monday has its own four rows with its own percentages. No week is inferred by this export.
The Program sheet is one row per exercise-per-day-per-week: rows 2-204, columns A-N, no merges, no hidden rows, no second block.
Row 206 is a colour legend, not program data: A206 "Mon Bench+Squat", C206 "Tue Deadlift", E206 "Thu Press day (all volume)", G206 "Fri Speed/hack", I206 "Sun Back/arms/core", K206 "Deload wk".
Saturday is never present as a row (it is a rest day). Wednesday appears only as the recovery walk.
restTime is null on every set: the sheet has no rest column and gives only one prose range (60-90s) for speed pulls.
set type is "working" on every set: the sheet marks no warmup, drop, or back-off sets at the set level.
The 93 accessory rows with no weight column at all are exported as load kind "rpe", since target RPE is genuinely the entire prescription for those rows.
